metadata.note: The New York, Ontario and Western Railway -- the 'Old and Weary', and the first major American railroad to be abandoned in its entirety. Its predecessor the New York and Oswego Midland Railroad was chartered in 1866 under DeWitt C. Littlejohn to link the docks opposite New York City with Lake Ontario at Oswego; construction north of Middletown began 1868 and the line was completed in 1873, only for the Panic of 1873 to bankrupt it. Reorganized as the O&W in 1880, it never owned rails into New York City: from 1883 it reached Weehawken Terminal over the New York, West Shore and Buffalo (later New York Central) from a connection at Cornwall-on-Hudson, so that stretch is deliberately NOT drawn here (see west_shore_railroad.geojson). The 1890 Scranton Division made it an anthracite hauler; milk from the Delaware, Chenango and Unadilla valleys and summer resort crowds bound for Sullivan County and the Catskills carried the rest. New Haven control from October 1904 under J.P. Morgan's 'Morganization' left it neglected; it entered receivership in 1937 and never left. Anthracite heating died, milk went to trucks, highways took the resort traffic. Last passenger train Roscoe - Weehawken September 10 1953; last freight Norwich - Middletown March 29 1957; rail and bridges lifted 1958-1959. GEOMETRY IS A REAL TRACE, not the waypoint approximation used elsewhere in this dataset: assembled from OpenStreetMap relation 2053379 ('New York, Ontario & Western Railway', 637 members), whose ways follow the surviving right-of-way as abandoned railway, rail trail and O&W-named roads. The 493 resolvable member ways were assigned to named lines by proximity to a corridor built from geocoded station towns, re-chained by node connectivity, de-duplicated where parallel trackage overlapped, and simplified to a 40 m tolerance. Straight-line bridges span gaps where OSM has no trace -- the largest are 19 km between Norwich and Randallsville on the main line, 12 km between Clinton and Utica on the Utica branch, 7 km at each end of the Port Jervis branch, and 6 km between Carbondale and Jermyn on the Scranton Division.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: Frequencies for every era and every branch are estimated. Individual branch abandonment dates are NOT sourced: several branches almost certainly went before the system-wide 1957 shutdown (cuts to the Monticello and Kingston branches were already being sought around 1940-41, and the New Berlin branch was sold to the Unadilla Valley Railway at an undetermined date), but every branch here is drawn as lasting to 1957 for want of confirmed dates. The Delhi branch is omitted entirely -- OSM relation 2053379 carries only about 6 km of it in two disjoint fragments. The Sylvan Beach loop north of Oneida is folded into the main line rather than drawn separately. The exact junction point of the Monticello branch at Valley Junction is approximated, so the lower few miles of the Monticello and Port Jervis branches may be attributed to the wrong one. NEW BERLIN BRANCH: the date the last passenger train ran on it is NOT sourced. The feature ends at 1941 because that is when the O&W sold the branch to the Unadilla Valley Railway -- an upper bound on O&W passenger service, not a documented passenger end date. Given that branch passenger traffic collapsed with improved roads in the 1930s, the true last passenger year is probably earlier than 1941, and the 1870 construction date is itself given only as 'circa 1870'. Sources also disagree on the sale year: 1941 in most accounts, 1940 in one.
metadata.freight_only_audit: 2026-08-24: removed as part of a repo-wide freight-only audit. Removed here: segment 1953-1957 from nyow-main-line (explicitly 'Freight only'; last passenger train Sept 10 1953). REPO RULE: this map shows PASSENGER rail only. Freight-only operation is not represented -- a line's segments must end when its passenger service ends. See CONVENTIONS.md.
metadata.new_berlin_branch_audit: 2026-08-24: the New Berlin Branch was previously a single feature dated 1889-1957, which was wrong on three counts -- the branch was built circa 1870 (not 1889), reached Edmeston in 1895 (not 'by 1889'), and left O&W ownership in 1941 (not 1957). It is now split into nyom-new-berlin-branch (1870-1895, New Berlin Junction to New Berlin under the New York and Oswego Midland) and nyow-new-berlin-branch (1895-1941, extended to Edmeston under the O&W). The Unadilla Valley Railway era, 1941-1960, is DELIBERATELY NOT DRAWN: the UV had ended its own passenger service by roughly the early 1930s and ran the ex-O&W branch as a freight/dairy line, so under the repo's passenger-only rule (see ../CLAUDE.md) those years do not belong on the map.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: An original New York and Oswego Midland branch, built from New Berlin Junction just north of Sidney up the Unadilla valley to New Berlin circa 1870. A dairy line: it carried the valley's milk down to the main line, and its passengers with it. The NY&OM went bankrupt in the Panic of 1873 and was reorganized as the O&W in 1880, which kept working the branch. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: Extended north from New Berlin to Edmeston in 1895, after the Wharton Valley Railroad agreed to lease its line to the NY&OM -- 29 miles in all from New Berlin Junction. The O&W worked it as a milk branch out of the Unadilla valley. Improved roads gutted the traffic in the 1930s, and the O&W sold the whole branch to the Unadilla Valley Railway in 1941. NOTE: 1941 is the OWNERSHIP end, not a documented last passenger train -- see the layer's not_yet_sourced field. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
